articles.title: A comet, a dim eclipse, and some red blueberries
articles.summary: The article discusses the newly discovered Comet C/2012 S1 (ISON), a potential sun-grazer predicted to offer a spectacular show in late 2013, while cautioning against overly optimistic predictions due to comet unpredictability. It also provides a detailed November 2012 observing guide, covering visible planets like Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune, and Mars, including a discussion of Mars's unique 'blueberry' spherules. Additionally, it highlights an upcoming penumbral lunar eclipse and other general astronomy news for the month.

articles.title: Messier Half-Marathon
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) successfully hosted a "Half Messier Marathon" at Henry Coe State Park on October 13, an event initiated by member Teruo Utsumi. Designed to engage new, inexperienced members with a manageable observing project and foster community, the gathering brought together over twenty-five participants for a BBQ, star-hopping, and deep-sky observation. Despite muted sky conditions, the event was lauded as a great success, reigniting club camaraderie and providing new observers with a positive dark-sky experience, with plans for a second half next spring.

articles.title: NASA Space Place
articles.summary: This article describes a meeting of an international team of astronomers analyzing data from the Herschel Infrared Observatory. They are investigating potential new types of icy and rocky debris disks around nearby stars, identified through anomalous bolometer readings. The team faces the challenge of confirming these discoveries by differentiating them from background galaxies, all while under pressure to publish before the data becomes publicly accessible in January.

articles.title: The Last Month in Astronomy
articles.summary: This astronomy update from October and September 2012 covers various space missions and scientific discoveries. Highlights include the Dragon spacecraft's resupply mission to the ISS, NASA's Deep Impact probe re-targeting an asteroid, and the discovery of dry ice snow in Venus's atmosphere. Significant advancements were made in cosmology with a more accurate measurement of the Hubble constant using the Spitzer telescope, alongside observations of a new X-ray nova and insights into the Milky Way's hot gas halo.

articles.title: SJAA Club Programs and Activities
articles.summary: This article details the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) recent activities and programs, including solar viewing at a festival, a general meeting with a guest speaker, and an Imaging Special Interest Group session. It also highlights the revamped telescope loaner program, the successful school star party initiative, and provides organizational contacts and publication information for the "SJAA Ephemeris" newsletter.
